vectors.name: quote-tier-recovers-an-edited-block
vectors.note: The QUOTE tier's positive case, which the corpus had no normative vector for. 'ing' lost its marker and had a word inserted, so marker and hash both miss; it recovers at 0.9865 (body 0.9365 plus the full 0.05 of context) against a runner-up of 0.2586. 'dlq' survived verbatim and short-circuits at the hash tier, so the vector also pins the ladder reaching QUOTE only when the stronger evidence fails. The score was 0.9822 through v1.2, when the stored suffix carried the whole 57-character neighbour against a candidate side windowed to 48 and so could only reach 0.0457 of its 0.05; §9 allows the selector 48 characters and windowing both sides restores it.

vectors.name: quote-prefix-supplies-the-margin
vectors.note: Two near-duplicate candidates 0.0097 apart on body score, which is under the 0.05 margin, so body-only scoring MUST detach. The stored prefix matches the preceding block of the better candidate and contributes the full 0.05 (§9's context bonus), lifting the margin to 0.0597 and committing to block 2. An implementation that applies the commit rule to body score rather than to the aggregate score fails this vector.

vectors.name: quote-context-lifts-the-best-over-the-threshold
vectors.note: The threshold half of the same question. The only real candidate scores 24/49 = 0.4898 on body alone, below §9's 0.5, so body-only scoring detaches however large the gap to the runner-up. The three vectors above pin the context bonus against the margin; this one pins it against the threshold.

vectors.name: quote-context-outranks-a-better-body-match
vectors.note: Ranking is by aggregate score, not by body score with context used only as a tiebreak afterwards. Block 0 is the better body match (40/44 = 0.9091); block 2 is worse (40/45 = 0.8889) but sits between both stored neighbours and takes the full 0.10, reaching 0.9889 against 0.9243. The commit goes to block 2, the block that loses on body. No score exceeds 1.0 here, so the outcome does not involve the clamp. An implementation that ranks on body and consults context only to break a tie commits to block 0 or detaches; either way it fails.

vectors.name: quote-near-duplicate-not-identical-commits-on-context-alone
vectors.note: The reachable near-duplicate hazard. Two byte-identical candidates that both differ from the quote, so their body scores are exactly equal (0.9358) and no body-score difference exists to decide between them: context is the whole reason one is chosen. The favoured candidate's raw aggregate is 1.0358, which the reported score clamps to 1.0, leaving a guarded margin of 0.0525 over the other twin's 0.9475. The corpus's other near-duplicate vector (near-dup-twins-detach-despite-high-score) is the identical-twin case, where both candidates reach 1.0 on body alone and the clamp leaves no margin at all. Here the id commits, which is what §9 permits when it allows up to 0.05 per side against a 0.05 margin.

vectors.name: quote-single-candidate-has-a-runner-up-of-zero
vectors.note: One surviving block, so there is no runner-up at all. §9's commit rule still applies and an absent runner-up scores 0, not undefined: the best clears the threshold and the margin is the whole score, so the id commits. An implementation that reads 'beats the runner-up' as presupposing a second candidate, and refuses to commit without one, detaches here.

vectors.name: quote-surviving-half-of-a-split-block-recovers
vectors.note: §9's split case: the block was cut in two and the quote is the whole original, so a surviving half is a strict substring of it. The half scores 2*20/(40+20) = 2/3, comfortably over the threshold, and recovers. This is the guarantee §9 describes when it says a surviving half must not 'score arbitrarily low'. Note that the containment floor §9 names for the job cannot be what delivers it: under containment the metric already returns 2s/(s+l), which exceeds the floor's s/l for every l > s, so the floor never raises a score. The guarantee holds; the named mechanism is inert.

vectors.name: quote-exact-tie-selects-the-later-candidate
vectors.note: Two byte-identical candidates score exactly equal, so under the default margin the guard always refuses and which one ranks first is unobservable. With the margin injected as 0 the selection becomes visible, and it must be the LATER candidate, which is what the score category already requires of `best_match` (conformance/spec/score.json, exact-tie case). This carries that rule up to the resolve level, where an implementation sorting stably from the front would otherwise pick block 0 unseen.

vectors.name: quote-normalization-is-ascii-only
vectors.note: §9 folds ASCII case only, so 'CAFE' with an acute accent and its lowercase form are NOT the same string: they score 0.9412, not 1.0. An implementation using Unicode casefold (or `\s` for whitespace, which matches U+00A0 where §9's set does not) scores 1.0 here and reports a different number. The fold is pinned this way precisely so two implementations agree without carrying Unicode case tables, and this is the resolve-level vector for it; the score and seqmatch categories cover the metric on non-ASCII input but not the fold inside a resolution.
